title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

errors: No outright mathematical error on this page; it is a programmatic statement whose content depends on conditions C1–C7 not yet formulated.

The claimed equivalence (𝔉, ≤, ≪) ⇔ (M, 𝔉_M) is asserted, not proved here. It rests on p.27, where a marginal note already corrects the corollary: 'Ce n'est pas vrai, il faut que la relation R_F soit plus petite…'. So the characterization of ≤ in terms of Umb and the equivalence relations was still in flux.
The symbol ≤ is first crossed out in the triple and then reinstated, indicating hesitation over whether ≤ is part of the axiomatized data.

ideas.what: Representation of an abstract structure of figures (𝔉, ≤, ≪) as a concrete family 𝔉_M ⊂ Fig(M) ⊂ 𝔓𝔓(M) over a 'point set' M of strata
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorem of Stone/Birkhoff type; concrete realization of abstract stratification data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936), Birkhoff (1937) for the order-theoretic prototypes
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; only the general programme of tame topology / stratified structures appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Viewing structures as elements of iterated power sets 𝔓𝔓𝔓(M) and naming them '(grande) multiaxiomatique'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki, Théorie des ensembles ch. IV

ideas.what: Strata = irreducible closed sets with generic point, in bijection with M via x ↦ closure of x (next page, Ax*1)
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology on a poset / sober T0 space; specialization order
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. S. Alexandrov (1937); sobriety in EGA / SGA4
ideas.where_published: EGA I (specialization, generic points); SGA4 (sober spaces) — general notions only

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to give a complete axiomatization (conditions C1–C7, Ax*1…) of 'figures' in a set of strata M as a combinatorial foundation for analysis situs / tame topology. This 1986 axiomatic framework does not appear in the tame-topology or stratified-spaces literature (o-minimality, Lurie's exit-path stratified spaces, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka).
missed.quote: (𝔉, ≤, ≪) s'interprète comme une "axiomatisation" de Fig(M) … satisfaisant certaines conditions (qui deviendront demain C1 à C7)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A poset-based, purely combinatorial axiomatics of stratifications could be compared with modern poset-stratified spaces (stratifications as maps to Alexandrov posets). It would be historically interesting to know whether Grothendieck anticipated that viewpoint. On this page, however, the content is only programmatic.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a transitional scholium: it states that the abstract figure structure is equivalent to concrete data (M, 𝔉_M ∈ 𝔓𝔓𝔓(M)) and announces axioms. The order-theoretic content is standard. The interest lies only in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic approach to stratified analysis situs.
transcription_corrections: 'F ⟼ Mod[?](F)' should most likely read 'F ⟼ Umb(F)', matching Umb on p.27 and Omb on p.29; the handwriting shows 'Umb(F)' with an initial loop.
'(𝔉, [-≤-], ≪)': in the image the middle symbol is crossed out in the first line but present in the second line '(𝔉, ≤, ≪)'.
'notation plus et un nom plus lapidaire': the first 'plus' appears to be struck out, giving 'une notation [-plus-] et un nom plus lapidaire'.

'figures ensemblistes dans M' is followed by an insertion '[en termes de]'. The phrase 'les raisons' is doubtful; it probably reads 'les conditions' or 'les axiomes' ('Je distinguerais par Ax*1 etc les … en termes de (M, 𝔉_M ∈ 𝔓𝔓𝔓(M))').

Bottom: a crossed-out 'Ax*1' in the left margin before 'Il est entendu que…', and 'Ax*1' underlined/crossed near 'que les élts de 𝔉_M'. The final word 'Conditions' is preceded by a struck 'Ainsi', with a small struck 'AE' above it.
